requestBody.description: Exactly one of chatId/contactId/phoneNumber/username identifies the recipient. Upload a single file as `file`, or several as repeated `files` parts.

messageType.description: MessageType — 2 Image, 4 Audio, 5 Voice, 6 Video, 7 Document. Derived from the file when absent.

files.description: Every attachment of a multi-file message (replaces `file` when present)

post.summary: Send a message carrying one or more uploaded files
A page of a channel’s activity log
A page of a channel’s webhook delivery log

200.description: The file’s bytes. The content type is the FILE’s own, not this declaration: a stored object can be any media type, so the schema is binary and the response header names the real one.

get.summary: Serve a stored file’s bytes (public — no api key, downloads on demand)

platform.description: The platform this instance speaks to

platformName.description: That platform’s name, for a label

qrCode.description: The first pairing QR as a data-URL, or null for a platform that does not pair by QR

platformId.description: The account the channel is connected as (own JID / user_id)
The account this channel is connected AS (its own JID / user id); empty until paired

state.description: Open (6) is connected; AuthenticateRequired (3) is waiting for a QR scan

raiseEvents.description: Publish events for this channel onto the queue

logWebhook.description: Record every webhook delivery in the webhook log

qrCode.description: The pairing QR as a data-URL, while one is outstanding

clusterNodeId.description: Which node of a provider cluster holds the session

syncHistory.description: Import existing chats and messages from the platform

config.description: Per-platform settings. Secret-named keys are sealed at rest and never answered.

platformId.description: The identifier the platform treats as primary

altPlatformId.description: The second identifier for the same human

source.description: Where the platform asserted the pairing

total.description: How many channels exist, not how many this page holds

credentials.description: Deep-merged over the stored credentials: objects merge, arrays and scalars replace

sessionUpdated.description: A running session took the change now; otherwise it applies on the next connect

qrCode.description: A fresh QR, or null when the channel is not awaiting pairing

platformId.description: The platform's user id (JID / user_id); matches the alt id too
The platform’s id for this person

altPlatformId.description: The platform’s second id for the same person (a WhatsApp privacy LID)

storedName.description: The address-book name, when it differs

username.description: The platform handle, where it has one

hasAvatar.description: Whether the platform has an avatar for them; null while unknown

email.description: Set where the platform knows one

total.description: How many the channel holds, not how many this page returns

count.description: How many contacts the import stored

mimeType.description: The stored file’s media type, as the message (or the avatar convention) declares it

filename.description: The file’s own name where the message carried one; absent for an avatar

storagePath.description: The object-store key the bytes live under

url.description: The path that serves the bytes on this provider’s HTTP port. A PATH, not an absolute URL: the provider does not know the host it is reached on, so join it to the base you called.

publicName.description: The display name to store for this contact. The platform is NOT told.

platformId.description: The platform's chat id (JID / chat_id); matches the alt id too

example.vcard:
BEGIN:VCARD
VERSION:3.0
FN:John Doe
TEL;type=CELL;waid=989121234567:+98 912 123 4567
END:VCARD

metadata.description: Per-platform side channel, e.g. { email: { to, cc, bcc, subject } }

count.description: How many people reacted with it

isChosen.description: The connected account is one of them

messageId.description: The platform id of the message being quoted

from.description: Who called, as a platform id

offline.description: The call arrived while the session was offline

contactId.description: The sender as an IDENTITY: the stored row carries the sender’s platform id here (the column’s name is historical). Empty for an outbound message, and empty for a room member who is not a counterpart.

senderPlatformId.description: ATTRIBUTION, not identity — who sent this, for display only. Set on a group / channel message, left unset in a one-to-one chat where the name comes from the chat’s own contact.

senderName.description: The sender’s display name, for the same display-only purpose as senderPlatformId

deletionReason.description: Why it is gone, when the platform says

mediaCachedAt.description: Set the moment this message’s media was pulled into permanent storage. From then on the attachment can never be expired again, so a reader must stop gating it behind a download click.

rawMessage.description: The platform’s own payload, serialised, when the channel retains it

platformId.description: The platform’s id for this conversation

contactPlatformId.description: The counterpart’s contact platform id, for a one-to-one chat whose own platformId is not the counterpart (an email thread is keyed by its root Message-ID). Unset where the chat id IS the peer id.

unreadMessages.description: Unread count as the provider counts it

lastMessage.description: The preview row this chat shows, when it has one

allowedReactions.description: The reactions this chat accepts, when the platform limits them

counterpartIsAutomated.description: The one-to-one counterpart is an automated account (a bot): a conversation whose counterpart is never a contact. Unset while the provider has not established it, and for groups.

participants.description: The roster as platform ids; `chats/get-participants` answers the joined rows

count.description: How many chats the import stored

contactId.description: Our contact row id for this member

role.description: The member’s role in the chat

platformId.description: The member’s platform id, joined in from the contact row — what puts a name on a group message, since a message names its sender by platform id and not by our UUID.

altPlatformId.description: What makes a LID-addressed message match a phone-JID-keyed contact

platformId.description: The platform's message id, as carried on every provider event

nextCursor.description: Pass it back as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last one

total.description: How many messages the chat holds

historyLoading.description: A background history fetch for this chat is running, so more is on its way — it arrives on the MessageSync event, and ChatHistoryLoaded says it finished. `messages/history` always answers false: it reads the stored rows and never starts a fetch.

messages.description: The file-bearing messages themselves — a file IS a message here, not a separate record

vcard.example:
BEGIN:VCARD
VERSION:3.0
FN:John Doe
TEL;type=CELL;waid=989121234567:+98 912 123 4567
END:VCARD

message.description: The edited row, or null when the platform accepted the edit and we hold no row for it

id.description: The provider’s row id, once persisted

contactPlatformId.description: The sender as an IDENTITY CLAIM — central resolves it into a contact and a person, so it is set only for a sender who belongs in the customer’s CRM.

senderPlatformId.description: ATTRIBUTION, not identity: who sent this, for display only. Never reaches contact creation.

nextCursor.description: Pass it back to continue the history walk; absent when the platform has no more

messages.description: One per target chat, in the order they were given

data.description: Whatever the entry carried; shape is the writer’s own

status.description: The delivery’s own status (WebhookStatusType), or the HTTP status it ended on

attempts.description: How many times it has been tried
